summary: Read docs/r3-panel-brief.md in full, then inspected the connected process-lifecycle source: src/library.rs:509-523 (restart_swaybg thread spawn), :525-591 (restart_swaybg_inner: pgrep -x, pidfd_open, /proc/pid/cmdline, owns_swaybg_args gate, pidfd_send_signal loop, start_swaybg), :593-616 (open_pidfd/read_cmdline), :610-616 (owns_swaybg_args), :618-637 (setsid -f sh -c 'sleep 0.3; exec swaybg ...'), :638-674 (4 argv unit tests), :692-737 (apply_wallpaper rename/verify/save_config_keys/restart order), tools/dictation/scripts/dictation_supervisor.sh (all 63 lines), tools/dictation/src/main.rs:55-115,168-171,303-348, src/hk.rs:195-206,402-412,428-436, src/output.rs, src/groq.rs:17, plus the callers at src/main.rs:5027-5061,5254-5290,6920-6923 and ~/.config/mango/autostart.sh:59-60,69-79. Repo verified: worktree HEAD abe9f5c with eb40eee an ancestor and `git diff eb40eee..HEAD` touching only COUNCIL_LOG.md and docs/reviews/r3/*.json, so the reviewed sources are identical at both heads. Ran: `cargo test --release --offline swaybg_ownership_tests` → 4 passed / 329 filtered; `bash -n` on the supervisor → clean (shellcheck not installed). Built /tmp-only reproductions: (a) supervisor lock inherited by the child — after SIGKILL of a supervisor the orphan child keeps fd 9, /proc/locks still shows the FLOCK, and a fresh supervisor prints "another supervisor holds ...; exiting" with rc=0; same during graceful TERM teardown while the child lags; (b) a faithful replica of the apply path layering two instances when two applies land inside the 0.3 s start window (1 instance on a single apply, 2 at 80 ms); (c) a Rust repro of `Command::spawn()` without wait leaving 3 zombies (SIGCHLD is not ignored on the live island: SigIgn=[1,3,13]); (d) a zombie's /proc/PID/cmdline is 0 bytes; (e) `setsid -f` with the inner exec failing exits 127 and produces no process and no log line. Live facts used read-only: swaybg PID 1608 argv is exactly the 5 tokens owns_swaybg_args accepts; supervisor 1632 predates the flock commit and holds no lock fd; child 2145 holds the log fd; ~/.cache/static-dictation.log is mode 600, 102059 B after 18 h 30 m (≈5.6 KB/h); island 15556 has one child (mmsg) and SIGCHLD is not ignored. No live wallpaper restart, supervisor restart, signal, socket, mic or capture was performed; no desktop process was touched, and the /tmp test processes were cleaned up. Verdict: the ownership design is genuinely careful (pidfd pinning, argv vetting, fail-closed enumeration, atomic copy + byte verify + strict persist order, private rotated log, single-instance lock, honest `shortcut:` comments), and the argv tests are real. But in this lens three lifecycle paths are still fire-and-forget or silent: the restart is never verified, the lock can be held by an orphan child that makes the replacement supervisor a silent no-op, and the 1 MiB rotation has no bound for a child that never exits. Combined with the 300 ms duplicate-instance window and unreaped children, this is not shippable at 9 under a process-lifecycle lens; 7 matches the earlier median.

findings.title: Wallpaper restart is fire-and-forget, unverified, and its real failure modes are silent
findings.detail: apply_wallpaper persists wallpaper=/theme= at src/library.rs:733 and then calls restart_swaybg() at :734, which spawns a detached named thread (:512-522) and returns nothing; the function then returns Ok(theme) unconditionally. start_swaybg (:618-637) nulls stdin/stdout/stderr and only reports `spawn()` failure of `setsid` itself, so a failure inside the shell — missing swaybg, a broken PATH, a compositor that refuses a second layer surface — exits 127 inside the child and prints nowhere. Observed: running the exact start_swaybg command line with a broken PATH exited 127, created no swaybg, and emitted no diagnostic; the child's stderr is /dev/null by construction. Nothing ever confirms the new instance is up: no waitpid, no pgrep of a fresh pid, no surface ack. Counterexample considered: the fail-closed branches (pgrep non-1 status, unreadable cmdline, foreign argv) do eprintln at :534,:538,:552,:560,:565,:585, and the island's stderr goes to /tmp/dynamite-r3-verified.log, so an operator can see those; but those lines are invisible to the user, apply_wallpaper has already returned Ok so src/main.rs:5027-5049 moves wall_selected/theme_selected and redraws as if it succeeded, and the spawn/shell-failure path prints nothing at all even to stderr. Result: the pill shows the new wallpaper selected while the screen keeps the old image, and the only way to notice is by eye. Fix: have restart_swaybg_inner block on the pidfd of each killed instance until it is reaped, then spawn, poll for a swaybg whose argv is the new (pidfd-pinned) instance with a bounded timeout, and return Result to apply_wallpaper so a failure can be surfaced instead of logged; capture the restart child's stderr to a small file rather than /dev/null.

findings.title: Supervisor lock is inherited by the child, so an abnormal supervisor death leaves a silently un-replaceable supervisor
findings.detail: tools/dictation/scripts/dictation_supervisor.sh:24 does `exec 9>"$LOCK"` and :25-28 exits 0 when the flock is taken; :58 starts the child as `"$BIN" >>"$LOG" 2>&1 &` without closing fd 9, so the child inherits the lock file descriptor (:53-59). Observed in /tmp: with a child started that way, both supervisor and child showed `9 -> .../static-dictation.lock`; after `kill -9` of the supervisor the orphan child still held fd 9, /proc/locks still listed `FLOCK ADVISORY WRITE`, and a new supervisor printed "another supervisor holds ...; exiting" and exited 0 — a silent no-op that looks like a successful start. The same window exists on a graceful stop: :44's trap kills the child and exits without waiting, and the child only acts on the flag at the top of its loop (tools/dictation/src/main.rs:168-171), while finalize() can be blocked in a 60 s groq POST (tools/dictation/src/main.rs:303-348; tools/dictation/src/groq.rs:17), so the lock stays held for up to a minute after the supervisor is gone. Observed with a TERM-lagging child: supervisor gone 1 s after TERM, child alive, flock still held, new supervisor exits 0 with "another supervisor holds". Counterexample considered: while the orphan child lives, dictation itself still works, so this is not an immediate outage; and ~/.config/mango/autostart.sh:74's `pgrep -f 'scripts/dictation_supervisor.sh'` guard would also block an automatic start. But once that orphan dies — or if the supervisor was the only wkilled process and the child exits on the next device error — nothing respawns dictation until the next login, which is the same failure class COUNCIL_LOG.md:145 already recorded and r2 #8c finding 4 raised. Fix: start the child with an explicit `9>&-` so the lock cannot be inherited, `wait` for the child after the trap's TERM (with a bounded escalation), and exit non-zero after a wait-for-lock timeout instead of exit 0 so a manual start is not silently swallowed.

findings.title: The 1 MiB log cap is unbounded for a child that never exits, and the live rate reaches the cap in about a week
findings.detail: rotate() runs only at the top of the supervisor loop (tools/dictation/scripts/dictation_supervisor.sh:48-54,57), i.e. after `wait "$child"` returns at :60, so the size check is unreachable while one child lives. The child is long-lived by design and re-logs every tracked key: tools/dictation/src/hk.rs:428-436 writes a line for every D/LEFTMETA/RIGHTMETA press and release (hk.rs:195-206), on top of every hold start/end and every transcription, all appending to the same fd. Measured live: ~/.cache/static-dictation.log is 102059 B / 1974 lines with the child up 18 h 30 m ≈ 5.6 KB/h, so the 1 MiB threshold is crossed after about 7.5 days of continuous uptime and the file then grows without any further check — there is no ceiling at 2 MiB, only a rotation that never fires. Counterexample considered: the code documents this exactly (`shortcut: one long-lived child can exceed 1 MiB until it exits; use an in-place monitor if sustained dictation logs grow too far`, :46-47), and the file is mode 600 with umask 077 (:15-18), so the privacy defect from COUNCIL_LOG.md:912 is fixed; the pre-flock supervisor still running (PID 1632, started 16:21, before commit 73a49df at 22:07) also means rotation is not even active on the live desktop yet. But the brief describes a rotation limit as delivered behaviour, and the honest reading is that the limit has no bound for the normal long-lived case. Fix: check the size from the child's own logging path (rate-limited in the binary), or run a tiny watchdog that rotates when the file exceeds the cap regardless of child lifetime.

findings.title: Two applies inside the 300 ms start window stack duplicate swaybg instances
findings.detail: start_swaybg waits 0.3 s inside the child before exec (src/library.rs:624 `sleep 0.3; exec swaybg ...`), while each apply runs its enumeration on a fresh detached thread (src/library.rs:512-522). Two applies closer together than that window both run `pgrep -x swaybg`, both see only the pre-existing instance, both SIGTERM it, and both then start a new one, so the second enumeration can never observe the first apply's not-yet-exec'd child. Observed with a faithful replica of :525-591 + :618-637 (pgrep -x, exact 5-argv check on the /proc cmdline, SIGTERM the vetted pid, then the same 0.3 s sleep+exec): one apply → 1 instance; two applies 80 ms apart → 2 instances, both with the identical accepted argv. Trigger in the real UI: src/main.rs:5259-5263 and :5284-5289 both apply on Enter and the panel is not disabled between presses, so a quick double-tap or a repeated key lands inside the window. Consequence is bounded — two identical fullscreen layers (~7 MB PSS each) draw the same image, and the next apply kills both because both match the argv gate — so this is not a permanent leak, but it does mean the round's "restart only our instances" invariant is not actually sequential. Fix: serialize apply with a mutex or an AtomicBool guard around restart_swaybg_inner and coalesce to the latest requested image, or drop the 0.3 s pre-exec sleep (retry the exec instead) so the new instance exists before the enumeration window closes.

findings.title: Every detached spawn leaks one zombie child because nothing reaps
findings.detail: src/library.rs:618-636 spawns `setsid -f sh -c ...` and drops the Child without waiting, and src/main.rs:2270-2276 does the same for the launcher's `sh -c` command; there is no waitpid, no SIGCHLD handler and no `signal(SIGCHLD, SIG_IGN)` anywhere in src/ (grep for waitpid/SIGCHLD/reap finds only the specific child.wait() calls in clipboard_panel, controlcenter, music, tray and wallpaper_blur). The live island's /proc/15556/status shows SigIgn=[1,3,13], i.e. SIGCHLD is not ignored. Verified with an isolated Rust repro of exactly `Command::new("setsid").args(["-f","sh","-c","exit 0"])...spawn()` with the Child dropped: 3 zombies appeared under the repro process and stayed. The direct child here is `setsid` itself, so the zombie on this system is named `setsid`/`sh`, not swaybg (which is why `ps --ppid 15556` is clean after a 1 h 10 m island uptime with no apply). Impact is small and bounded by usage, but it is a permanent per-apply/per-launch kernel entry that no code path ever reaps. Fix: `drop` the setsid child after an explicit `child.wait()` in the worker thread (it exits immediately because of -f), or install a reaper.

findings.title: Only one exact 5-argument swaybg form is treated as ours, so a slight variation silently disables the whole feature
findings.detail: owns_swaybg_args (src/library.rs:610-616) requires argv.length==5 with argv[1]=="-i", argv[2]==the exact wallpaper.png path, argv[3]=="-m", argv[4]=="fill". ~/.config/mango/autostart.sh:59-60 happens to produce exactly that (verified: live PID 1608 argv is byte-for-byte the accepted form), but any other launch — a manual `swaybg -m stretch`, a `-o eDP-1` selector, a second image used for one session, or a path written with a symlinked $HOME — makes :564-568 print "foreign swaybg is running; leaving wallpaper processes alone" and return, so every wallpaper apply becomes a no-op that still reports success through :734-736. Counterexample considered: this is deliberate fail-closed behaviour and is the safer direction than killing an unknown process; but it is indistinguishable from a successful restart to the user, and the message goes only to the island's log. Fix: accept any argv whose `-i` value resolves to the same file (canonicalize both sides) and whose mode is recognized, leaving genuinely different images/processes alone.

findings.title: A defunct swaybg is misclassified as a foreign process, blocking the restart while it exists
findings.detail: src/library.rs:555-563 reads /proc/<pid>/cmdline and only treats `ErrorKind::NotFound` as "gone, skip". A killed but unreaped swaybg still appears in `pgrep -x swaybg` (verified: after SIGKILL of a test process, `pgrep -x` listed the pid 23765 while `ps` showed state Z), but its /proc/<pid>/cmdline is 0 bytes (measured: `stat -c %s` → 0, and reading it yields an empty argument list). read_cmdline then returns Ok(empty vec) at :603-607, owns_swaybg_args is false, and :564-568 returns "foreign swaybg is running" — so a zombie suppresses the restart rather than being skipped. The window is short (swaybg is started via `setsid -f`, so it is normally reparented to the session supervisor and reaped), which is why I rate it minor, but the code does not distinguish "no argv yet / defunct" from "someone else's process". Fix: treat a zero-length cmdline (or state Z from /proc/<pid>/stat) as "not ours, skip" with `continue` rather than aborting the whole apply.

findings.title: The reviewed supervisor lock and rotation are not in force on the running desktop
findings.detail: Live supervisor PID 1632 was started 2026-11-19 16:21:19, before the flock/rotation commit 73a49df (2026-11-19 22:07:02), so it holds no lock descriptor (`ls /proc/1632/fd` shows only 0,1,2,255) and /proc/locks has no entry for the lock inode; its child 2145 has fd 9 on /dev/input/event18, not the lock. ~/.config/mango/autostart.sh:74 guards on `pgrep -f 'scripts/dictation_supervisor.sh'`, which matches the old process, so the new single-instance and rotation code stays dormant until the next login. This is a deployment observation, not a code defect, but it means the round's lifecycle fixes are unexercised on the host the reviewer is judging. Fix: mention in the closing note that a logout is required, or make the supervisor exit when its own script mtime/content is newer than its start time so a respawn picks up the new version.

findings.title: The kill loop can leave the desktop with no wallpaper at all
findings.detail: src/library.rs:572-589 signals the vetted pids in a loop and returns on the first non-ESRCH error, which abandons the remaining kills and skips start_swaybg at :590. The validation phase is genuinely all-or-nothing (every pid is checked before any signal), but the signal phase is not: a single EPERM/ENOSYS-style failure after an earlier pid was already SIGTERMed leaves zero swaybg instances and the bare root colour until the next successful apply. Counterexample considered: pidfd_send_signal with an already-open pidfd and a same-uid target essentially only fails with EPERM (impossible for our own child) or ESRCH (handled), so the trigger is narrow; but the failure mode is the worst possible one (no wallpaper instead of old or new), and it is silently indistinguishable from success for the caller. Fix: on failure, stop suppressing and go straight to start_swaybg (better a duplicate than a blank screen), or retry with SIGKILL on the pidfds and only then abort.

what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the wallpaper apply path verified rather than fire-and-forget: have restart_swaybg_inner wait on each killed instance's pidfd until it is reaped, then spawn and poll with a bounded timeout for a swaybg whose argv matches the new image, capture that child's stderr to a file instead of /dev/null, and return Result so src/main.rs:5027-5049 only moves wall_selected/theme_selected after a confirmed restart (otherwise report it in the pill). Serialize apply with a mutex or AtomicBool so the 300 ms pre-exec window cannot stack instances, and drop or replace that sleep with an exec retry. In the supervisor, close the inherited lock descriptor for the child (`"$BIN" ... 9>&-`), wait for the child after the TERM trap with a bounded escalation, and exit non-zero on lock contention so a manual start is not a silent no-op. Replace the between-children rotation with a check that also fires while the child lives (rate-limited rotation from the binary, or a watchdog), so the 1 MiB cap is a real ceiling. Reap the setsid/launcher children (wait on the immediate setsid child, which exits at once) so nothing z zombies permanently. Accept any argv whose `-i` resolves to the same image and with a recognized mode, and skip defunct/zero-length cmdlines instead of aborting. Finally, note the required logout so the live supervisor actually runs the locked, rotating version under review.
